headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Devin’s broad workspace/network/tool access can ingest and act on Cognee outputs without a documented verification boundary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can use MCP, browsers, shell, and shared integrations, so if Cognee outputs are passed into its workspace or tickets, prompt-like content could steer actions. Cognee’s session-memory CLI and data-processing role make it plausible it emits content Devin may consume. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF Cognee output is copied into Devin’s workspace, Slack, Jira, or MCP inputs without sanitization, injection risk is present.
IF Devin parses Cognee-generated text as instructions rather than data, the pathway is active.
mitigations: Add a strict instruction/data delimiter in all handoffs.
Strip or escape markdown, code fences, and imperative phrases before transfer.
Route Cognee outputs through a human review step for high-risk tasks.
Disable MCP ingestion for untrusted Cognee artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and parser hardening.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cognee touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents, while Devin has broad network egress, cloud workspace files, and third-party integrations. If the pair shares files or tickets, Devin can transmit sensitive content to GitHub, Slack, Jira, Notion, or MCP endpoints. That creates a default exfiltration path with potentially irreversible disclosure.
conditions: IF Cognee data classes are placed into Devin-accessible files or integrations, leakage risk exists.
IF Devin is connected to any external API while handling those files, exfiltration is possible.
mitigations: Keep Cognee and Devin on separate workspaces.
Remove sensitive fields before any transfer to Devin.
Disable Devin integrations for sensitive projects.
Use a redaction pass on support, finance, and personal data.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP and per-dataset access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cognee supports multiple instances with agentic user/tenant isolation, but Devin can write files, modify git state, and run parallel sessions with shared integrations. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can race and overwrite each other. The profiles show overlapping mutable surfaces, so conflict is plausible in default collaborative setups.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or cloud workspace, file and git conflicts can occur.
IF Devin uses shared integrations while Cognee updates related artifacts, race conditions are active.
mitigations: Assign separate repos or branches per agent.
Freeze git writes during Cognee runs.
Use a single-writer policy for shared files.
Review and merge changes manually before commit.
requires-engineering: add locking or transactional coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cognee produces documents, decisions, workflows, and SQL-related outputs, and Devin’s autonomous planner-executor model can act on external inputs across shell, browser, and integrations. If Devin treats Cognee output as authoritative, errors can cascade into commits, tickets, or messages without verification. The interaction is not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF Devin consumes Cognee-generated facts or workflows without a verification step, cascading error risk exists.
IF Devin is allowed to commit, message, or ticket based on Cognee output, downstream impact is amplified.
mitigations: Require a verification checklist before Devin acts on Cognee output.
Limit Devin to draft-only mode for Cognee-derived tasks.
Add human approval before commits or external messages.
Compare Cognee outputs against source documents before execution.
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating and provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while Devin handles cloud workspace files and integrations with third-party services. If regulated data flows from Cognee into Devin’s cloud workspace or external APIs, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not document a specific mismatch, so this is a plausible compliance exposure rather than a confirmed violation.
conditions: IF personal data or finance data from Cognee is routed into Devin integrations, compliance review is required.
IF the deployment involves regulated data with retention or residency constraints, policy mismatch risk exists.
mitigations: Classify data before handing it to Devin.
Exclude regulated records from Devin workflows.
Set shorter retention on shared artifacts.
Review vendor DPAs and residency settings.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention enforcement.
